name: Motion Garden
description: Illustrated rehabilitation service deck with goal maps, patient support diagrams and editable process graphics.

slides.title: MOTION
items: GARDEN

Rehabilitation built around
everyday goals
Illustrative service presentation

slides.title: Everyday goals shape the conversation
items: A person arrives with a life to return to. The service records what matters to them, then connects that goal to the plan agreed with their clinician.
The first conversation
What would you like to do more easily? What support do you already have? What would make appointments easier to attend?

slides.title: A plan has four connected parts
items: PERSONAL GOAL
Daily activity
Describe the task that matters to the person.
Clinical plan
Record the plan agreed with the treating professional.
Practical support
Agree access, appointment and communication needs.
Review point
Set a date to discuss progress and revise the plan.

slides.title: The first visit creates a shared record
items: Listen
Capture the person’s priorities in their own words. Record any support needed for the appointment.
Agree
The clinician and patient agree the next step and how it will be reviewed.
The illustration shows a service conversation, with no exercise instructions.

slides.title: The pathway has a place for review
items: First contact
Understand the referral and arrange the first conversation.
Shared plan
Record the agreed goal, appointments and review point.
Review together
Discuss what has changed and record the next agreed action.
The timing and clinical content follow the local service pathway.

slides.title: One cohort, three appointment needs
items: Synthetic snapshot of 60 people
In-person visits
Appointment at the clinic with access requirements recorded.
Remote reviews
Planned conversations using the service’s agreed remote channel.
Home visits
Locally agreed visits with travel time included in the schedule.

slides.title: The service plans around real journeys
items: Before the visit
Agree the location, transport and communication needs.
During the visit
Make room for questions and check the shared record.
After the visit
Provide the agreed next step and a contact for queries.

slides.title: Progress needs a consistent question
items: Synthetic responses to “I understand my next step”
A communication measure
Each survey asks the same question after the review. Compare response counts as well as the share of positive answers.
40 responses per round. This example measures understanding of the plan.

slides.title: The person stays at the centre
items: PERSON
Treating clinician
Agrees and reviews the clinical plan.
Coordinator
Arranges appointments and tracks open queries.
Chosen supporter
Joins discussions when the person wishes.
Receiving team
Receives the agreed handover at transition.

slides.title: A complete handover answers four questions
items: What matters?
The personal goal is clear enough for the next team to discuss.
What was agreed?
The current plan and its review date are recorded.
Who owns the next step?
A named service or professional accepts the handover.
How can the person ask?
The person has the contact details for queries about the plan.

slides.title: The pilot builds capacity in stages
items: Month 1
Map the current service and rehearse the shared record with staff.
Month 2
Open a small cohort and review every unresolved handover.
Month 3
Review access, communication and workload before adding capacity.

slides.title: The weekly review keeps work visible
items: Open referrals
People awaiting the first agreed appointment.
Active plans
People with a current plan and a scheduled review.
Handovers due
Transitions requiring confirmation from the receiving team.
Synthetic operational snapshot. These categories may overlap and should be reviewed separately.

slides.title: A pilot with a clear decision point
items: Illustrative three-month budget

£75k staff capacity
£45k access and coordination
£30k evaluation and training
The decision
Expand only after the team reviews patient communication, completed handovers and the workload required to sustain the service.

slides.title: Every plan belongs to a person
items: A rehabilitation service proposal
The pilot connects everyday goals with a shared record, an agreed review point and an accountable handover.
Fictional service and synthetic data. Illustrations show service conversations. Clinical plans follow local practice.
